purpose: Repeatable editorial evaluations for international technical readers. Assertions concern meaning and protected artifacts, not exact preferred phrasing.
method: For an inline case, give a fresh evaluator only the request and input, plus the skill. For a fixture case, copy the complete fixture.source_dir, relative to this file, into a new scratch directory while preserving its layout, then materialize each fixture.seed_files mapping at that relative path in scratch, creating parent directories as needed. Use the fixture metadata to prepare and collect the run, but give the evaluator only the request, resulting artifact tree, and skill. Do not expose the fixture metadata, allowlisted_files, assertions, or a model answer. Review every assertion against the source; check protected code, anchors, link targets, identifiers, obligations, facts, and repository publication evidence. Do not execute documented commands. Style checks do not establish deployed behavior.

cases.request: Rewrite this overview for an international technical audience. Keep the supported scope and publication status.
cases.input:
# Component overview

This section provides context for this Building Block. Our cutting-edge solution gets teams up to speed and is a game changer for integrations.

The Building Block Specification defines a common response format for record reads. Independent Building Block Software implementations use that format. Without a common format, an integrating client needs a different response mapping for each implementation. The specification defines the interface; it does not provide a running service.

This document is a draft. No deployed conformance result is available.
assertions: The overview starts with the technical reader problem or purpose, rather than boilerplate, idioms, or promotional claims.
The distinction between Building Block Specification and Building Block Software, the common response format, and the client mapping consequence remain accurate.
The draft status, absence of deployed conformance evidence, and absence of a running service remain explicit.
No claim of achieved savings, automatic interoperability, certification, or new software functionality is added.

cases.request: Edit this reference prose for clarity without changing obligations, classifiers, identifiers, anchors, or links.
cases.input: # Record reads ## Requirement 4 `REQUIRED IMMUTABLE` When a caller requests a retained revision, the implementation MUST evaluate the caller's current disclosure rights before returning that revision. It MUST NOT substitute current state when the retained revision is unavailable. The client MAY retry the request only while its access token remains valid. See [revision selection](#revision-selection). ## Revision selection This section describes revision selection. Revision identifiers are source-backed and opaque.
assertions: The condition, subject, action, and before-return constraint of Requirement 4 remain explicit.
Current disclosure rights, retained revision, and the prohibition on substituting current state are preserved.
MUST, MUST NOT, MAY, and the retry token-validity condition keep their force and scope.
REQUIRED IMMUTABLE, req-4, revision-selection anchors, and the Markdown link target are identical.
No new requirement, actor, identifier, or rationale is introduced without evidence.

cases.request: Rewrite this how-to as clear instructions for a technical reader. This is a documentation edit; do not execute its commands.
cases.input:
# Validate an API description

The reader should first make sure Node.js and the repository dependencies are available. From the repository root, it is then necessary to run the following command:

```sh
node tools/check-api.mjs api/openapi.yaml
```

An exit status of 0 means that the configured structural checks pass. It does not demonstrate deployed behavior. If the command reports an error, read its finding and correct the API description before running the command again.
assertions: The result uses imperative instructions in the established order, with prerequisites and repository-root context retained.
The command text is byte-for-byte identical after accounting for Markdown list indentation, and no example command is executed as part of the writing task.
The success criterion remains exit status 0 for configured structural checks only, with deployed behavior explicitly unverified.
No dependency version, install command, fix, successful run, or deployment result is invented.
Tool and file names needed to perform the task are retained despite a general preference against implementation details in reference prose.

cases.request: Improve the scope explanation using only the established ownership and rationale in the supplied text.
cases.input:
# Scope

The scope of this document is about record retrieval. The Consultation API returns permitted record views. The shared authorization policy determines which fields a caller may receive; that policy is owned by the authorization service and is outside this API description.

The interface returns the same public error for an absent or protected Record. This prevents the response from revealing whether the protected Record exists.
assertions: The scope clearly names record retrieval and permitted views.
The out-of-scope authorization policy and its known owner are retained without inventing a link, another component, or policy mechanics.
The existing protected-existence rationale remains connected to the shared public error, not broadened into a universal security or legal claim.
No decision-maker marketing rationale or new API operation is added.

It is not a deployed implementation. ```yaml openapi: 3.1.0 info: title: Reference API version: 1.0.0 paths: /records: get: operationId: getRecords description: Keep this embedded description unchanged. responses: '200': description: Keep this response text unchanged. ``` Use the `Authorization` header as defined in [the authentication profile](#authentication-profile). The source example value is `03/04/2026`; its interpretation is not specified. Do not infer a calendar date from it. ## Authentication profile The profile is a draft and has no implementation evidence.

Authorization, operationId getRecords, the authentication-profile anchor, and the Markdown link target remain identical.

The draft and illustrative status and lack of deployment evidence are retained.

cases.request: Edit the text for an international technical audience while preserving established technical meanings. Report any unresolved claims separately.
cases.input:
# Request processing

The service authenticates the client certificate before it evaluates the caller's authorization. Authentication and authorization are separate checks. TLS 1.3 is the declared transport version.

If possible, the service handles all requests, etc. A request may use name and/or status. The source does not define the fallback behavior or whether those filters are conjunctive or disjunctive.
assertions: Authentication, authorization, the client certificate, their ordering, and TLS 1.3 remain technically precise.
The editor does not replace technical concepts with vague synonyms merely to shorten the text.
The editor does not infer fallback behavior, completeness guarantees, or AND/OR matching semantics.
Review notes flag the ambiguous phrases and their missing evidence; canonical unresolved statements remain unresolved.
No region-specific metaphor, local legal assumption, or invented terminology is introduced.

cases.request: Rewrite this assessment for international technical readers. Keep the requirement, observation, interpretation, and proposal distinct, without resolving the mismatch.
cases.input: # Retained-history assessment The adopted reference requires that when retained history is unavailable, the implementation MUST NOT substitute current state. A local regression test returned current state when retained history was unavailable. This observation is limited to the local test environment. No production validation has run. This suggests a mismatch between the implementation and [the requirement](#req-7). The requirement has not changed. The proposal is to investigate the fallback, then add a regression case only after the owner confirms the cause. No fix has been applied.
assertions: The adopted MUST NOT requirement and its unavailable-history condition remain unchanged in meaning.
The local test result remains observed evidence, not an authorized change to the reference behavior or a deployed conformance result.
The apparent mismatch remains an interpretation to investigate; no cause, fix, or revised policy is invented.
Investigation remains proposed, and the regression case remains conditional on owner confirmation after that investigation. No applied fix or production validation is claimed.
The req-7 anchor and its Markdown link target are preserved.
